answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to a bonded collateral escrow and links evidence of coordinated equivocation across identities. If k identities equivocate together, the correlated penalty scales as O(k²); detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier, such as e^(αk) for α>0, so a swarm risks far more than isolated actors. Asymmetric depreciation makes recovered collateral worth less, while a thread of shared evidence can send a ripple through the lagoon of linked claims.
